report_name: CHAINDROP Worm Compromises Over 1,300 NPM Packages

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The CHAINDROP worm compromised the 'keyv' npm package and used its maintainer's credentials to inject malicious code into over 1,300 dependent packages.

attack_patterns.name: User Execution
attack_patterns.description: The malware is executed when a developer runs `npm install` on a project containing a compromised package, triggering the malicious `preinstall` script.

attack_patterns.name: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: The CHAINDROP worm's payload is a JavaScript file (e.g., `Math_Symbol.js`) executed by Node.js via a `preinstall` script in the `package.json` file.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The malware payload searches the compromised system for sensitive credentials in files such as `.npmrc`, `.git-credentials`, and AWS configuration files.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Password Stores
attack_patterns.description: The CHAINDROP malware steals developer credentials for services like npm and GitHub from various configuration files on the compromised system.

malware.name: CHAINDROP
malware.description: A self-propagating worm, identified as a variant of Shai-Hulud, that executed a massive supply-chain attack on the npm ecosystem. It steals developer credentials and uses them to spread to other packages.

malware.name: Shai-Hulud
malware.description: A malware family from which the CHAINDROP worm is derived.

campaigns.name: CHAINDROP
campaigns.description: A widespread, automated software supply chain attack using the CHAINDROP worm to compromise over 1,300 npm packages, starting with 'keyv'. The campaign aims to steal developer credentials for npm, GitHub, and AWS. Malicious commits associated with the campaign used the author name 'claude' and commit message 'chore: update config'.

identities.name: npm
identities.description: The npm software package ecosystem was the target of the CHAINDROP supply chain attack, with over 1,300 packages compromised.

identities.name: GitHub
identities.description: Developer credentials for GitHub were a primary target for theft by the CHAINDROP malware.

identities.name: AWS
identities.description: Developer credentials for AWS were a primary target for theft by the CHAINDROP malware.

indicators.name: CHAINDROP Malicious Payload Filenames
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: CHAINDROP Malicious Payload File Creation
id: 7c5a1b9e-8d0f-4b2c-9a1d-3e4f5a6b7c8d
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of files with names used by the CHAINDROP npm worm.
references:
  - https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/shai-hulud-chaindrop-npm-supply-chain
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-07
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Math_Symbol.js'
      - '\math_init.js'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of malicious JavaScript files used by the CHAINDROP worm.

indicators.name: CHAINDROP Payload Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: CHAINDROP Malicious Payload Execution
id: f1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of malicious JavaScript files associated with the CHAINDROP npm worm, often via a `preinstall` script.
references:
  - https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/shai-hulud-chaindrop-npm-supply-chain
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-07
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '\node.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Math_Symbol.js'
      - 'math_init.js'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the CHAINDROP payload script `Math_Symbol.js` or `math_init.js` using Node.js.

indicators.name: Suspicious NPM Preinstall Script Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious NPM Preinstall Script Execution
id: a0b1c2d3-e4f5-4a6b-7c8d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects a suspicious process chain where npm executes a script via node.js from within a node_modules directory, a TTP used by CHAINDROP.
references:
  - https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/shai-hulud-chaindrop-npm-supply-chain
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-07
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '/npm'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '/node'
    CommandLine|contains: 'node_modules'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate packages that use preinstall or postinstall scripts.
indicators.description: Detects the execution of a script from a `node_modules` directory by `npm`, a behavior leveraged by the CHAINDROP worm's `preinstall` hook.
